findings.comment: Easement call-outs use abbreviated forms ('Elec. Esm't.', 'Elec. & Tele.', 'P.U.E.') rather than complete proper nomenclature. Please revise all easement labels on the plat and all plan sheets to use complete proper nomenclature, such as 'Electric distribution, electric telecommunications, and electric fiber easement' or 'Public Utility Easement for electric distribution.'
applicableAreas: Plat and all plan sheets showing electric easements
findings.observation: Examined the plat sheet (Sheet 2) and the electrical design plan (Sheet 21) for easement nomenclature. Vision analysis of Sheet 2 identified: 'Easement labeled on Plat: "Exist. 5' Elec. Esm't." (Uses abbreviations for Existing, Electric, and Easement).' Vision analysis of Sheet 21 identified easement labels as: '"5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 385 D.R.T.C.Tx."' (uses abbreviated form 'Elec.') and '"5' P.U.E."' (abbreviated). No instances of complete proper nomenclature such as 'Electric distribution, electric telecommunications, and electric fiber easement' or full spelling of 'Electric Easement' were found. All easement labels observed use abbreviated forms.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 specifies that easements must be 'clearly delineated on plans' with proper nomenclature. The grouping guidance identifies 'abbreviated forms ("ETE," "EE") rather than complete proper nomenclature (e.g., "Electric distribution, electric telecommunications, and electric fiber easement")' as a common violation pattern indicating non-compliance. The intent is to ensure clarity and prevent confusion about which utilities are actually served by an easement. Use of abbreviations like 'Elec.' and 'Esm't.' fails to meet the 'complete proper nomenclature' standard. The applicant has presented abbreviated labels throughout the site plan documents.

findings.comment: All electric easement labels use abbreviated forms ('Elec.', 'Tele.', 'Ease.') rather than complete proper nomenclature. Update all easement labels on site plan, plat, grading plan, and electrical design plan to read 'Electric distribution, electric telecommunications, and electric fiber easement' with the appropriate width designation (e.g., '5' Electric distribution, electric telecommunications, and electric fiber easement').
applicableAreas: All electric easement labels shown on Sheets 2, 9, 11, and 21
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) reveals electric easements labeled as: 'Elec. Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14 Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx.' and '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 385 D.R.T.C.Tx.' Sheet 2 (Plat) shows easements labeled '3' Elec. Ease.' and 'Exist 5' Elec. Ease.' Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows '5' Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14 Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx.' and '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 883 O.P.R.T.C.Tx.' Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) similarly shows '5' Elec. Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14 / Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx.' and '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 885 D.R.T.C.Tx.' All instances use abbreviated terminology: 'Elec.' for Electric, 'Tele.' for Telephone, 'P.U.E.' for Public Utility Easement, and 'Ease.' for Easement. The full proper nomenclature 'Electric distribution, electric telecommunications, and electric fiber easement' is not used on any sheet.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 (Application Requirements for Austin Energy Land Development Review) requires that easements serving electric facilities be clearly and properly labeled. The grouping specifically identifies that abbreviated forms (ETE, EE, Elec. Easement) are non-compliant and must be replaced with complete proper nomenclature. The plans consistently use abbreviated terminology across four sheets, indicating a systematic nomenclature deficiency rather than isolated labeling error. The abbreviations fail to convey the complete scope and type of utilities accommodated within the easements (distribution, telecommunications, fiber).

findings.comment: Easement call-outs use abbreviated forms (e.g., 'Elec. Easement,' 'Elec. & Tele. Easement,' 'P.U.E.') rather than complete proper nomenclature. Revise all easement labels to use complete designations, for example: 'Electric distribution, electric telecommunications, and electric fiber easement' or equivalent full nomenclature that clearly identifies all facilities authorized within each easement.
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Site Plan (Sheet 9) and Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) reveals the following easement labels: 'Top boundary: 5' P.U.E. Vol. 69, Pg. 14 Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.T.x.'; 'Right boundary (upper): 5' Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14 Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.T.x.'; 'Right boundary (lower): 5' Elec. Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14 Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.T.x.'; 'Far right edge (bottom): 5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5068, Pg. 883 D.R.T.C.T.x.' All easement labels use abbreviated nomenclature ('Elec.' instead of 'Electric', 'Tele.' instead of 'Telecommunications', 'P.U.E.' instead of full spelling) rather than complete proper nomenclature.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that 'Easements are clearly delineated on plans' with proper nomenclature and designations. The grouping's regulatory overview explicitly states: 'Plans must explicitly designate easements...generic easement labels are insufficient.' The use of abbreviated forms ('EE,' 'ETE,' 'Elec.') violates this requirement because abbreviated forms do not clearly communicate the full scope of utilities authorized within the easement. Complete proper nomenclature such as 'Electric distribution, electric telecommunications, and electric fiber easement' ensures clarity about which utilities are present and their respective clearance requirements. Abbreviations create ambiguity about facility types and can lead to compliance verification errors.

findings.comment: Electric easements not designated as aerial or non-aerial. Specify each easement as 'Aerial Electric Easement' (for overhead poles, conductors, guys) or 'Non-Aerial Electric Easement' (for underground conduit, pad-mounted equipment) to establish correct clearance and access requirements per UCM § 1.10.3 (aerial) and § 1.10.4 (non-aerial).
findings.observation: Sheets 2, 9, and 21 show five foot electric easements labeled generically as '5' Elec. Ease.' or '5' Electric Easement' without designation as aerial (for overhead facilities) or non-aerial (for underground facilities). Vision analysis found: two 5' electric easements on the plat; two 5' electric easements on Sheet 9; easement references on Sheet 21. No easement label specifies whether it accommodates overhead distribution lines/poles/guy wires (aerial) or underground conduit/pad-mounted equipment (non-aerial), despite the fact that Sheet 21 shows both overhead line on west boundary and underground infrastructure throughout site.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires that easements be clearly designated as to their function. Aerial easements must provide vertical clearance and lateral space for poles, conductors, and guy anchors; non-aerial easements must provide subsurface space for conduit and equipment pads with horizontal clearances. Without explicit designation, it is unclear whether shown easement dimensions are adequate for the type of infrastructure occupying them, and whether access, height, and clearance requirements are satisfied.

findings.comment: Plans do not distinguish between aerial and underground electric easements. Please designate each electric easement as either 'Aerial Electric Easement' (for overhead facilities: poles, conductors, guys, with required vertical clearances) or 'Underground Electric Easement' (for subsurface facilities: conduit, pad-mounted equipment) on all plan sheets showing easements.
findings.observation: Examined electric easement labels on Sheets 9, 11, 21. The 5' electric easements are labeled as '5' Electric Easement Vol. 73, Pg. 76' or '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 883' but have NO designation indicating whether they accommodate aerial (overhead) or non-aerial (underground) facilities. Sheet 21 shows existing overhead lines (OHE) and existing underground lines but the easements are not explicitly designated as 'Aerial' or 'Underground.' Per UCM § 1.10.0, aerial easements require vertical clearance maintenance (7.5 ft horizontal, 15 ft radius); underground easements require subsurface clearance from other utilities. The failure to distinguish prevents verification of correct easement type.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires plans to 'distinguish between aerial electric easements and underground electric easements.' This is not a formatting preference but a regulatory requirement because aerial and underground easements have different clearance, maintenance, and access requirements per UCM §§ 1.10.3 and 1.10.4. Aerial easements accommodate poles, overhead conductors, guys, and require tree-free zones and vertical clearances. Underground easements accommodate conduit, pad-mounted equipment, and require different horizontal clearances. Without designation, it is unclear what uses are permitted within each easement, and AE staff cannot verify the design accommodates the correct infrastructure.

findings.comment: Electrical easements not distinguished as aerial vs. underground. Label all electrical easements to specify whether they accommodate aerial facilities (overhead poles, conductors, guy wires) or underground facilities (conduits, pad-mounted equipment, buried laterals), and ensure clearance requirements are applied appropriately to each type.
applicableAreas: Plans showing electrical easements - Site Plan (Sheet 9), Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), Plat (Sheet 2), Landscape Plan (Sheet 31), Grading Plan (Sheet 11)
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 2 (Plat) vision analysis: Easements are shown with width dimensions (5' P.U.E., 5' Elec. & Tel. Easement, 5' Elec. Easement) but the vision analysis explicitly states: 'No. The labels on the plat do not contain the words "aerial," "overhead," or "underground."' Sheet 21 vision analysis confirms: 'Existing easements are shown (as noted above). However, the labels do not explicitly distinguish between "aerial" or "underground" within the easement text itself (they are generally labeled "P.U.E." or "Elec. & Tele. Easement"). The lines running through or near some of these easements are labeled "OHE" (Overhead Electric), implying aerial use in those specific areas, but the easement labels themselves do not make this distinction.' Sheet 9 vision analysis notes: '5' Electric Easement is labeled along the right (eastern) property boundary' and '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement labeled near the bottom right' but no distinction of type. Both aerial (overhead conductors, poles, service drops, guy wires) and underground (conduit, pad-mounted transformers) electric infrastructure exist on this site. The regulatory overview explicitly distinguishes these: 'Aerial electric easements accommodate overhead facilities... with vertical sky-to-ground clearance requirements; non-aerial easements accommodate underground facilities... with horizontal and subsurface clearance requirements.' Without this distinction labeled on easements, plan reviewers cannot verify that clearances and access are adequate for the actual facility type using each easement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires plans to show 'All public and private easements (electrical, gas, water, sewer, telecommunications, drainage) with locations and extents clearly delineated.' The grouping's Code References section (lines 72-90) identifies UCM § 1.10.3 and § 1.10.4 as establishing different clearance requirements for aerial vs. non-aerial easements. The Regulatory Overview specifically states: 'Plans must distinguish between: Aerial vs. Non-Aerial Easements: Aerial electric easements accommodate overhead facilities (poles, overhead conductors, service drops, guy wires) with vertical sky-to-ground clearance requirements (7.5 ft horizontal, 15-ft radius); non-aerial easements accommodate underground facilities (conduit, pad-mounted transformers, underground laterals).' Without this distinction labeled on the plans themselves, it is impossible to verify that clearances meet requirements for the type of facility in each easement. Both overhead and underground facilities are shown on this site (OHE lines on Sheet 21, underground conduits on Sheet 21), confirming that both easement types exist.

findings.comment: Add transmission notes to Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) referencing the detailed transmission clearance and access requirements shown on the general notes sheet, or verify that transmission facilities do not exist and remove transmission notes from Sheet 3 if inapplicable.
applicableAreas: Transmission easement area (if transmission facilities present on site)
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) contains an extensive "Electric Transmission Notes" section with 16 numbered items covering transmission clearances, digging restrictions, access requirements, and construction safety. However, examination of Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows no transmission-related notes—only standard utility easement references and general drainage/construction notes. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) likewise contains no transmission-related notes; the blocks shown reference only irrigation notes, general landscape notes, and legend definitions, with no text addressing transmission facilities, clearance zones, or construction restrictions related to transmission.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(8) requires that transmission notes be included on "coversheet, note page, grading plans, and landscape sheets when transmission facilities are present." The presence of comprehensive transmission notes on Sheet 3 suggests transmission facilities exist on or immediately adjacent to the site. Transmission facilities have substantially different access and construction restrictions than distribution facilities and require special contractor awareness and coordination with Austin Energy (per the 16 transmission notes on Sheet 3, including 48-hour pre-construction safety meeting, 25-foot clearance from structures, OSHA 20-foot clearance from energized lines, etc.). Contractors and workers reviewing the grading plan or landscape plan would have no awareness of these transmission-specific constraints, which creates a safety and compliance risk.

findings.comment: Resolve transmission facility status: Either transmission structures are present on or adjacent to the site (in which case they must be clearly documented on the existing conditions survey and transmission clearance compliance must be demonstrated), or transmission notes in Sheet 3 Block 20 should be removed per UCM § 1.16.0(8) requirements that notes match actual site conditions.
applicableAreas: Plat notes and general notes on cover sheet and grading/landscape plans
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes), Block 20 includes 16 detailed 'Electric Transmission Notes' referencing transmission structures, transmission easements, transmission wire, and access requirements (e.g., 25-foot clearance zones, 48-hour pre-construction meetings, 46,000 lb tandem axle road support, fire hydrants 20+ feet from transmission). Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) does not show any transmission structures or lattice towers—only standard distribution poles are visible. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) does not show any transmission infrastructure. Facts.md confirms the site is outside the 100-year floodplain and within a typical urban context.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(8) requires that transmission notes appear on cover sheets, plat notes, grading plans, and landscape plans ONLY when transmission facilities (60kV+, large structures) are present on the site. Conversely, these notes must be REMOVED if no transmission facilities exist. The applicant has included 16 transmission-specific notes (Block 20 on Sheet 3) but has not clearly documented whether transmission facilities exist. The existing conditions survey does not show transmission structures. If transmission does not exist, the notes should be removed. If transmission does exist, it must be clearly documented on the existing conditions survey and the plans must demonstrate compliance with transmission clearance requirements.

findings.comment: Transmission notes appear on coversheet (Sheet 3) but no transmission structures or transmission easements are evident on electrical plan or utility plan. Clarify whether transmission facilities (60kV+ voltage level) are present on or adjacent to the site. If no transmission facilities exist, remove transmission notes from coversheet, grading plan, and landscape plan per UCM § 1.16.0(8). If transmission facilities do exist, ensure all required transmission notes appear on all applicable sheets.
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes / Coversheet) contains detailed Electric Transmission Notes in Block 20, including 16 specific notes about transmission line clearances, safety meetings, barricading, access, and structural load requirements. These notes appear on the coversheet. The utility plan (Sheet 21) shows OHE (overhead electric) facilities marked as dashed lines along property boundaries. However, the vision analysis of the electrical plan and visual examination of other sheets indicate that the OHE shown on the property boundaries appear to be DISTRIBUTION facilities (poles and conductors along the boundary), NOT TRANSMISSION facilities (large steel transmission structures with 60kV+ voltage). The site plan does not depict any transmission line easement boundaries, transmission structures, or transmission-specific infrastructure. The checklist item requires determining: (1) whether transmission facilities exist, and if they do, transmission notes must be present on coversheet, grading plan, and landscape plan; or (2) if transmission does NOT exist, transmission notes should be removed. The extensive transmission notes currently on the coversheet suggest transmission facilities were expected but may not actually exist, or the engineer included them as a standard template.
findings.reasoning: The grouping distinguishes between 'transmission' (60kV+ voltage, large structures, transmission easements) and 'distribution' (less than 60kV, typical pole-mounted infrastructure). The presence of transmission notes on the coversheet suggests the design team anticipated transmission facilities on or near the site. However, visual review of the electrical plan and other documents shows only distribution facilities (OHE poles and conductors). The facts.md file did not identify any transmission easement or transmission structure on the property. This creates ambiguity: either (a) transmission facilities exist and are not properly depicted on plans, or (b) transmission notes were included as template language and should be removed. Without clear identification of whether transmission facilities are present, the status cannot be definitively 'pass' or 'fail'. The condition is UNCLEAR and requires clarification from the applicant regarding whether transmission infrastructure is present on or adjacent to the site.

findings.comment: Electric utility easements not clearly demonstrated or described on site plan. Verify that all existing and required electric utility easements are properly depicted on Sheet 2 (Plat) with dimensions, and provide metes and bounds descriptions for any additional easements required by Austin Energy for service installation and ongoing maintenance.
findings.observation: The facts.md documents multiple easements affecting the property, including electric easements. Sheet 2 is the Subdivision Plat which should show easement designations. However, review of the available documentation does not confirm that electric utility easements are clearly depicted with dimensions and labels on the plat, or that metes and bounds descriptions have been provided for any additional easements required by Austin Energy. The facts.md shows some easements are not depicted on the site plan and are missing from COA GIS layers.
findings.reasoning: Plans must demonstrate sufficient electric utility easements and provide metes and bounds descriptions for additional easements required by Austin Energy per UCM § 1.16.0(3). The facts.md specifically notes that some recorded easements are NOT depicted on the submitted site plan (Greenbelt and City of Austin Drainage easements). If electric easements are also not properly depicted or described, this represents a deficiency in demonstrating adequate easement areas and accessibility for AE operations and maintenance.

findings.comment: Electric utilities easements not dimensioned and metes and bounds descriptions not provided. Add dimensioned easement areas to site plan showing: (1) existing 5-foot electric easements from 1975 plat and their relationship to proposed improvements, (2) transmission easement boundaries with dimensions, and (3) any additional easements required for service feeds to buildings. For new easements required by Austin Energy, provide complete metes and bounds legal descriptions with bearings, distances, and reference points per survey control.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows proposed electric infrastructure (transformer pads, pull boxes, underground routing) but does not show electric utility easement areas or boundaries dimensioned on the plans. Facts.md indicates two recorded electric easements (5-foot each) from the 1975 plat (Vol 73/76, C8S-75-160), but their current location relative to proposed improvements is not confirmed on the site plan. Transmission easement requirements are documented (Sheet 3 Block 20) but easement boundary is not dimensioned or metes-and-bounds described on the electrical drawings.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(3) requires plans demonstrate sufficient electric utilities easements or provide metes and bounds descriptions for additional easements required by Austin Energy. Sheet 21 does not show existing electric easement locations/dimensions. Given the transmission line crossing and new service points to 8 buildings, additional easements will be required. The absence of dimensioned easement areas and metes-and-bounds descriptions for required easements is a deficiency.

findings.comment: Recording information for existing electric easements is provided on plans but is inconsistent across sheets and partially illegible. Clarify and standardize recording information for all existing easements, ensuring volume/page numbers and instrument numbers are clearly legible and consistent across all sheets showing easements.
findings.observation: Sheet 2 (Plat) shows two 5' electric easements with recording information that is partially illegible due to image resolution. Vision analysis indicates: '5' Elec. Ease' on north boundary of Lot 2 has no visible recording reference; '5' Elec. Ease' on south boundary of Lot 1 has unreadable text in Volume/Page format. Sheet 9 shows recording references more clearly: '5' Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14; Vol. 73, Pg. 76' and '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 883 D.R.T.C.Tx.' Sheet 21 references '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 385 D.R.T.C.Tx.' Facts.md documents two 5' easements from Mecey Subdivision (Vol. 73, Page 76). Recording information is present but inconsistent across sheets and partially unclear.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires that recording information (document number, volume/page, or plat reference) be provided for all existing electric easements. While recording citations appear on multiple sheets, the information is not consistently legible and references differ between sheets (Vol. 5468, Pg. 385 vs. Pg. 883), creating ambiguity about which easements are referenced and whether all easements are properly documented with complete recording information.

findings.comment: Recording information (volume/page, document number, or plat reference) not provided for existing electrical easements. Add recording information to all easement labels, cross-referencing the Travis County plat or deed document where the easement was recorded (e.g., 'Vol. 73, Pg. 76, Case C8S-75-160').
applicableAreas: All sheets showing electrical easements - Plat (Sheet 2), Site Plan (Sheet 9), Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), and others
findings.observation: Sheet 2 (Plat) vision analysis explicitly confirms: 'No. While there are volume and page references shown on the plat (in circles indicating adjacent property deed records, e.g., Vol. 3058 Pg. 2327), there are no specific Volume/Page references or document numbers attached directly to the easement labels themselves. The labels only indicate if they are "(Exist.)" or "(Existing)."' Sheet 21 vision analysis confirms easements are shown with labels like '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 385 D.R.T.C.Tx.' (which does have recording info on this sheet), but upon closer examination, sheet 9 shows '5' Electric Easement' and '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement' with no volume/page references shown. The facts.md document (lines 135-143) identifies several existing electric easements: '5' Electric Easements (×2)' with 'Document Ref: Travis County Doc 73/76, Case C8S-75-160' and '7.5' Public Utility Easement' with the same reference. These recorded documents should be cited on the plans. On Sheet 2, the plat does not include volume/page references for the electric easement labels, representing an omission of required recording information.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires easements to be shown 'with locations and extents clearly delineated.' The term 'clearly delineated' encompasses not only spatial location and width but also legal identification. The Regulatory Overview explicitly states: 'Recording information: Electric infrastructure documentation requirements... UCM § 1.16.0 serves as the comprehensive baseline for land development review applications, specifying what must be shown on plans to obtain Austin Energy approval.' LDC § 25-4-132 (cited in Code References) requires 'Easement dimensions, locations, and designations to match exactly between plat and site plan.' Without recording information (volume/page or document number), easement locations cannot be verified against recorded documents, overlapping or conflicting easements cannot be identified, and the legal identity of each easement is unclear. This is particularly important where multiple easements may exist on the same site (this site has at least 7-9 documented easements per facts.md). Recording information must appear on all plan sheets showing easements.

findings.comment: Transformer vault easements labeled on Sheet 21 but not formally depicted with boundaries, dimensions, or recorded document references as required for proper easement documentation
applicableAreas: Transformer pad vault easement areas (three transformer pads shown on Sheet 21)
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows three transformer pads on the site, with dashed rectangular boundaries around each transformer location. The western transformer pad near Building 8 has an explicit text label 'Vault Easement' visible via leader line. However, no formal easement boundary dimensions, area calculations, metes and bounds descriptions, or recorded document references are provided for these vault easements. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does not show these vault easements labeled or bounded. The surrounding off-site easements on both sheets are labeled with recording information (e.g., '5\' Elec. & Tele Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 885 D.R.T.C.T.S.'), but the on-site vault easements lack such formal documentation. The existing plat-dedicated 5-foot electric easement (from 1975 Mecey Subdivision) is shown on Sheet 11 but does not explicitly encompass the transformer pad locations, suggesting separate easement areas are needed for the vaults.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires that 'Electric easements [be] shown on site plan sheets for all Austin Energy facilities.' The term 'shown' implies clear identification with boundaries, dimensions, and reference information sufficient for recording and legal description. The vault easements are labeled but lack formal depiction with:  (1) Defined boundaries (only dashed rectangles without dimension callouts), (2) Area or width dimensions, (3) Metes and bounds descriptions or recorded document references, (4) Cross-referencing to any formal easement dedication or title document. The vision analysis of Sheet 21 explicitly notes: 'No specific dimensions (length/width) are marked for this vault easement.' Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does not show vault easements at all. This falls short of the requirement to 'show' easements on site plan sheets with sufficient clarity for Austin Energy to understand the extent of the dedicated area. The deficiency is the absence of formal easement boundaries and dimensions for the vault areas.

findings.comment: Applicant must provide one of the following: (1) Pavement Design Sheets certifying that all roads, driveways, and parking areas within transmission easements are designed to support 48,000 lb tandem axle loads with 5-foot spacing, including subgrade, base, and surface course calculations sealed by a registered engineer, OR (2) Revised site plan with a note explicitly stating that no roads, pavement, driveways, or parking areas are located within the transmission easement areas. Reference the 5-foot easement boundaries shown on Sheets 2 and 4.
applicableAreas: roads, driveways, pavement, parking areas, and any subsurface infrastructure within transmission easement (5-foot easement along north and south boundaries)
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) Electric Transmission Notes require: 'Roads/driveways/pavement/parking within the easement should be built to support a 46,000 lb tandem axle (5 foot spacing) to ensure safety.' UCM § 1.16.0 specifies 48,000 lbs as the most restrictive standard. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the site layout with proposed parking, driveways, and roadways. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows the grading throughout the site. Sheets 22-24 show construction details for driveways, curbs, and related infrastructure. However, NONE of these sheets provide pavement design calculations, load capacity certifications, or engineering documentation demonstrating that any surfaces within the transmission easement (5-foot easements along north and south boundaries) are designed and certified to support 48,000-pound tandem axle loads. There is no reference to pavement specifications, base courses, subgrade preparation, or structural design adequate for this load requirement.
findings.reasoning: The transmission easement requires that any pavement crossing or parallel to it must support 80,000-pound Condor trucks used by Austin Energy for maintenance. This is a structural design requirement, not merely a note. Per UCM § 1.14.4 and § 1.16.0, applicants must affirmatively demonstrate compliance through engineering calculations and design certification. The site plan does not provide this documentation. If any parking, driveway, or pavement is proposed within the 5-foot transmission easements, it must be designed accordingly. If no pavement is within the easements, this should be explicitly noted and shown on the plans.

findings.comment: Minimum 25-foot wide all-weather access route for vehicles to transmission easements not provided or shown on plans. General Notes reference extensive transmission facility requirements (25-foot clearances, transmission structures, transmission wires), but no 25-foot transmission access corridors are shown or dimensioned on the Site Plan. Clarify the presence and location of transmission easements and facilities. If transmission easements exist, provide a clear delineation of the 25-foot minimum access corridor with 16-foot vertical clearance, all-weather paved surface (HMAC or PCC), and specifications for gates, grades, and curbs as required by UCM § 1.14.4.
applicableAreas: Entire site, if transmission easements are present
findings.observation: General Notes (Sheet 3) contain extensive transmission facility requirements, including: 'Do not dig or grade within 25 feet of transmission structures,' '25-foot clearance from energized transmission lines,' 'Roads/driveways/pavement/parking within the easement should be built to support a 46,000 lb tandem axle,' and specific requirements for access corridors, gates (minimum 16 feet wide, 24-hour access), grades (no slopes greater than 8%), curbs (laydown curbs), and drainage restrictions. These transmission notes indicate that transmission facilities are either present on or immediately adjacent to the site. However, examination of the Site Plan (Sheet 9), Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), and Grading Plan (Sheet 11) reveals NO 25-foot-wide access corridors with 16-foot vertical clearance explicitly shown or dimensioned. The electric easements shown on the plans are only 5-foot, 7.5-foot, and 10-foot wide—far below the 25-foot transmission requirement. No transmission easement access routes are labeled or dimensioned with 25-foot widths.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.4.A specifies 'Access (Transmission Facilities): A minimum 25-foot wide all-weather access route for vehicles to transmission easements with 16 feet minimum vertical clearance.' The regulatory overview defines transmission facilities as 'energized at 60kV or higher' and notes 'The 100-foot proximity threshold triggers specialized transmission review requirements.' The General Notes on Sheet 3 extensively reference transmission structures, transmission wires, and transmission easements with specific 25-foot requirements, strongly indicating that transmission infrastructure exists on or adjacent to the property. However, the site plan shows only 5-foot to 10-foot easement widths and provides no evidence of 25-foot access corridors. This creates a critical gap: either transmission facilities do not exist on the site (contradicting the extensive transmission notes), or the required 25-foot access corridors have not been shown on the plans. Without 25-foot access corridors clearly delineated and dimensioned on the plans, the applicant cannot demonstrate compliance with UCM § 1.14.4.A.

findings.comment: Metes and bounds descriptions and surveyor-sealed field notes not provided for new electric easement dedications required for interior electrical routing and transformer pad locations. Applicant must submit surveyor-executed field notes and metes and bounds descriptions for all proposed electric easement areas to Austin Energy for review and approval prior to recordation.
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows proposed underground electrical lines routing extensively through the interior of the site, with four transformer pads located outside the historic 5-foot perimeter electric easements shown on the 1975 Mecey Subdivision plat. The electrical system design requires new utility easement areas to cover interior line routing and transformer pad footprints. However, no easement exhibits, surveyor-sealed field notes, metes and bounds descriptions, or separate instrument dedication documents are evident in the site plan set or supplementary documents. The Master Comment Report references Austin Energy review completed, but no coordination correspondence regarding easement dedications is included in the submittal. Facts.md notes (line 10) state 'Additional electric easements may be required at a later date,' indicating unresolved easement status. The existing 5-foot electric easements from the 1975 plat are insufficient for this project's proposed interior electrical infrastructure.
findings.reasoning: The project is filing a site plan (SP-2025-0126C) without a concurrent new subdivision plat, making EL-7.1 (plat dedication) inapplicable. Therefore, any new easements must be dedicated by separate instrument per Code § 14-1-21. The visual analysis of Sheet 21 confirms that proposed electrical facilities extend well beyond the historic 5-foot perimeter easements and require additional easement areas. Code § 14-1-22(A)(2)(b) and UCM § 1.16.0(3) mandate that metes and bounds descriptions with field notes signed, dated, and sealed by a surveyor must be provided to Austin Energy for review. The absence of these documents constitutes a failure to meet the separate instrument dedication requirement. The fact that easements are merely noted as 'may be required at a later date' indicates the applicant has not yet submitted the required surveyor-sealed documentation.

findings.comment: Existing electric easements are not shown on all required plan sheets. Please add electric easement depictions (with recording information and dimensions) to: (1) Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan); (2) Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan); (3) verify depiction on all other applicable sheets (site, grading, irrigation, storm drain, wet utility sheets).
applicableAreas: All plan sheets: site, utility, landscape, grading, irrigation, storm, wet utility
findings.observation: Examined all required plan sheets for electric easement depiction. Sheet 21 shows 5' electric easements with recording info on southern boundary. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows electric easements with citations on eastern and southern boundaries. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows electric easements on eastern and southern boundaries. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) has legend entry for electric in legend but vision found NO easements drawn on the plan itself. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does NOT show electric easements—only shows utilities W, SD, and OHE line. Per facts.md, there are TWO 5' electric easements from Mecey Subdivision plat (Vol 73, Pg 76) plus additional easements from Cortez Heights plat (Vol 64, Pg 13).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires existing electric easements to be shown 'on all required plan sheets' (site, utility, landscape, grading, irrigation, storm, wet utility). Current status: Easements shown on Sheets 9, 11, 21 but MISSING on Sheet 19 and Sheet 31. The incomplete depiction across all sheets means coordination cannot be verified—particularly Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) where trees must not conflict with easement access and maintenance. The omission from Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) creates inconsistency in the utility coordination across sheets.

findings.comment: Sheet 3 includes detailed Transmission Notes (16 items), yet transmission structures are not clearly shown on the Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4), and no building elevations are provided. If transmission facilities exist, building elevations must be provided showing transmission lines and demonstrating compliance with transmission clearance requirements. If transmission facilities do not exist, the transmission notes should be removed from Sheet 3.
applicableAreas: Transmission facility locations (if present on or adjacent to site)
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) includes Block 20 titled 'Electric Transmission Notes' containing 16 detailed requirements for transmission easements, clearances, and access (e.g., 25-foot clearance zones, 48-hour pre-construction meetings, 46,000 lb tandem axle road support). These notes explicitly reference transmission structures, transmission easements, and transmission wire. However, Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) does not show visible transmission structures (only standard distribution poles). The preliminary electrical design plan (Sheet 21) does not show transmission infrastructure. Despite the presence of transmission notes, no building elevations are provided that would demonstrate how proposed structures relate to transmission lines.
findings.reasoning: If transmission facilities are present on or adjacent to the site (as suggested by the inclusion of detailed transmission notes on Sheet 3), UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires that building elevations be provided 'showing transmission lines where applicable.' The applicant cannot demonstrate whether this requirement is met or not, because: (1) transmission structures are not clearly documented on the existing conditions survey, and (2) no building elevations are provided in the site plan set. The inclusion of transmission notes without corresponding transmission detail on the existing survey creates ambiguity.

findings.comment: Provide CAD file showing plan view of all building footprints overlaid on transmission line easement boundary with dimensions showing distances from transmission structures. Coordinate with Austin Energy to verify clearance compliance.
findings.observation: No transmission easement is shown on the site plans (Sheets 9 and 21), therefore no CAD overlay showing building footprints relative to transmission line easement can be verified. Multiple electric easements are labeled (5', 15' widths) on the property perimeter, but the transmission easement boundary is not depicted. Without the transmission easement depicted and building footprints overlaid, accurate clearance measurement cannot be performed.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.0 requires CAD files showing building footprint overlaid on transmission easement for accurate clearance verification when buildings encroach into easements. The absence of the transmission easement on the plans prevents verification of clearances. While this site shows electric easements, the transmission easement referenced in Sheet 3 coordination notes is not depicted, making it impossible to verify that buildings maintain required clearances from transmission structures.

findings.comment: Site plan not following UCM § 1.14.0 Transmission and Substation Requirements - transmission easement not depicted on working plans. Add transmission easement boundary to all relevant site plan sheets (Site Plan, Grading Plan, Electrical Design Plan) with dimensions and coordinates. Show 25-foot clearance zones from transmission structures. Demonstrate compliance with all transmission easement requirements on the plans, not just in general notes.
findings.observation: Sheet 3 contains comprehensive transmission and substation requirements per UCM § 1.14.0 with detailed notes on easement clearances, access provisions, grading restrictions, fencing coordination, and construction protocols. However, examination of Sheets 9, 11, and 21 (Site Plan, Grading Plan, and Electrical Design Plan) reveals that the transmission easement is NOT depicted on these working sheets. The transmission easement boundary is not shown on the site or grading plans where it is essential for design coordination. Transformer pads are shown but are not correlated with transmission easement requirements. The site plan layout does not explicitly demonstrate compliance with transmission easement requirements through visual representation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.0 Transmission and Substation Requirements mandate that sites with transmission facilities must follow specific design and coordination protocols. While the general notes on Sheet 3 reference these requirements, the actual site plan sheets do not demonstrate compliance through proper depiction of the transmission easement, clearance zones, and design accommodations. The transmission easement must be depicted on the working plans with dimensions and coordinates so that all designers (landscape, grading, electrical, site) can coordinate their work to maintain required clearances and access provisions.
